key_insight: Random Forest and XGBoost led shading-fault detection, but operating-condition differences limit how confidently their performance can be attributed to shading signatures.
engineering_relevance: Reliable rooftop PV fault monitoring requires episode-aware validation and matched no-fault sampling before selecting a classifier for deployment.
method: Compared seven classical and ensemble-tree classifiers on physically staged shading faults.
Used three repeats of five-fold, episode-grouped nested cross-validation.
Applied SMOTE within training folds and Holm-corrected pairwise significance tests.
evidence_signal: On 20,800 sensor rows retaining all 17 fault episodes from a 4 kW rooftop plant, Random Forest achieved mean accuracy of 0.838 and MCC of 0.526.
watch_item: Clock time alone reached MCC 0.44, indicating operating-condition confounding; Random Forest also almost entirely missed four fault episodes.
paper_title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data
